page: Microsoft Azure E16ps_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on Microsoft's ARM64 architecture using the Neoverse-N2 processor. The instance provides 16 dedicated physical cores running at 3.4 GHz with 1 thread per core, backed by 128 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 64 KB of L1 data cache. Memory provisioning sits at 128.0 GB of RAM, resulting in an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio with 8.0 GB allocated per core. The server includes no bundled local storage and operates without discrete GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results highlight exceptional memory throughput alongside stable general compute performance. Memory subsystems scored in the top tier (top 10%) on PassMark memory benchmarks, complemented by top 25% throughput in large-block read-only (308.13 GB/sec) and write (124.58 GB/sec) bandwidth tests. General computation scores, including Geekbench multi-core (14841.0) and single-core (1701.0), as well as stress-ng multi-core CPU metrics (33150.94), fall consistently into the middle 50% category. Large language model inference remains viable on smaller models with 607.25 tokens/sec prompt processing, though heavier models demonstrate weak relative throughput.

The architectural design offers strong qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound tasks due to the dense 128 GB memory footprint on power-efficient ARM silicon. A clear operational tradeoff is the complete absence of local disk drives, requiring remote network-attached premium storage volumes for persistent data. This hardware profile makes the instance particularly effective for in-memory databases, Redis deployments, data processing pipelines, and enterprise caching workloads that need substantial memory bandwidth rather than heavy vector-accelerated computation.
description: Microsoft Azure E16ps_v6 is an ARM-based memory-optimized instance featuring 16 dedicated Neoverse-N2 cores at 3.4 GHz and 128.0 GB of system memory. Operating without local storage or GPU acceleration, the virtual machine delivers an 8:1 memory-to-core allocation designed for memory-intensive workloads. Performance evaluations demonstrate top-tier memory metrics, highlighted by top 10% PassMark memory scores and top 25% large-block uncached memory read and write bandwidth. General-purpose CPU calculations perform in the median range across Geekbench and stress-ng suites. While medium-sized model inference exposes compute throughput limitations, the high-density RAM architecture offers favorable efficiency for caching tiers, Redis instances, in-memory databases, and large data processing pipelines.
